# MigrateProof

> Scans an existing test suite to find documented API response changes its
> assertions miss. The default workflow observes JSON fetched through
> `globalThis.fetch`, mutates responses, and reruns affected tests.

## What it is

A CLI that checks whether existing tests notice an API response change. It
does not define whether a business rule is correct. The scan runs the target's
`npm test` on the host and only observes JSON responses reached through
`globalThis.fetch`; unsupported or unconfirmed cases are **Cannot prove**.
The fixture workflow can replay a hand-stated invariant against recorded
responses when that narrower proof is needed.

## Commands

- `migrateproof [scan] [--changes <file>] [--json]` — scan tests against documented changes; without `--changes`, generate exploratory mutations.
- `migrateproof init <name> --method <M> --url <U>` — scaffold a new fixture.
- `migrateproof capture <fixture-dir> --as v1|v2 --url <U>|--from-file <path>` — record a response.
- `migrateproof replay <fixture-dir> --version v1|v2 [--json]` — replay it through the real consumer code and check the invariant.
- `migrateproof diagnose <fixture-dir>` — classify why a v2 replay failed, without Docker.
- `migrateproof patch <fixture-dir> --patch-backend codex` — ask a configured coding agent to propose a fix in an isolated Git worktree, then replay it. The worktree is not a security sandbox; agent execution has that tool's permissions. Never merges automatically.
- `migrateproof install-skill` — writes agent-readable setup instructions into the current repository at `.agents/skills/migrateproof/SKILL.md`.

## Fixture format

Three files per fixture: `fixture.yaml` (method, URL, recorded v1/v2
responses), `consumer.ts` (default-exported async function performing the
real call), `invariant.ts` (default-exported predicate over the result).
